title: He looked holy.
paragraphs:
He looked holy.
But heaven said: “I can’t use that heart.”

Because the scariest place to be…
is close to God—
yet completely unreachable by Him.

You can pray.
Serve.
Show up every Sunday.

And still have a heart
God resists.
Here’s the tension most people don’t want to face:

You don’t lose God because He moves away.
You lose Him because your heart hardens.

“I’m okay.”
“I know enough.”
“I don’t need to change.”

James 4:6 says:
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”

God doesn’t just ignore pride.
He opposes it.

You can be chasing God…
while God is resisting you.
And here’s where it gets dangerous.
Because pride doesn’t feel like rebellion.

You still look righteous.
You still speak the language.
You still carry the scroll.
Look at the man in the poster.

Hand on his chest.
Truth just hit him.
That moment where everything inside you says:
Some scholars interpret moments like this in Scripture through the lens of the Pharisees—men who knew the Law but missed the Lord.

Jesus said in Matthew 23:27:
“You are like whitewashed tombs… beautiful on the outside but full of dead bones inside.”

There’s hidden pride.
Unforgiveness.
Secret sin you’ve learned to manage instead of surrender.
That’s the heart God cannot use.

Not because He lacks power—
but because you won’t let Him in.
But here’s what most people miss…
God is not looking for perfection.

Psalm 51 17 says:
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”

Because the same God who resists the proud…
runs toward the humble.
And this is where Jesus steps in.
Every proud heart has a root:

Not just mistakes.
Not just bad habits.
A desire to be your own god.

Romans 3:23 says,
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
But God didn’t leave us there.

Romans 5:8 says,
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not after you fixed yourself.
Not after you got humble enough.

While you were still proud.
Still resisting.
Still running.
So your heart doesn’t have to stay hard.

Ezekiel 36:26:
“I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. I will remove the heart of stone… and give you a heart of flesh.”
But here’s the line you can’t ignore:

God gives new hearts…
to those who surrender the old one.
So the real question is not:

Are you willing to drop the pride?
To stop pretending?
To let conviction break you instead of defending yourself?
You don’t need to clean yourself up first.
Whisper it if you have to:

“Jesus… break my pride.
Give me a new heart.”
Because that’s what He died for.
If this hit you, don’t ignore it.

That weight you feel?
That’s not shame.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
